behavior: The web app reads and writes API data through Redux Toolkit and RTK Query, with the same screens and refresh behavior
acceptance: A store per tab and per signed-in user (store/store.ts makeStore, providers/store-provider.tsx) holds only the RTK Query cache; shared/api/api-slice.ts sets the base URL and Privy token; profiles, balances and activity inject their endpoints from their features; useLoad and the hand-written fetch client are gone.

Balances and activity read again every 15 s while the tab is visible and when it comes back; query arguments include the profile, so another profile's data never shows; a new profile joins the cached list without a refetch; a user change or ended session gives a fresh empty store; amounts stay exact strings.
Same screens and copy: lint, typecheck, unit, build, e2e and the live sign-in suite pass.
notes: 2026-10-10 review fail by reviewer: Cross-user cache leak when the Privy session ends without the Sign out button. apps/web/src/screens/app-shell/app-shell.tsx:46 caches POST /v1/me under one key (undefined) for every user, and resetApiState runs only in signOut (app-shell.tsx:63-67). StoreProvider lives in app/(app)/layout.tsx, which also wraps /sign-in, so the store survives the redirect. Scenario: A's session expires or is revoked (Privy sets authenticated=false), the shell redirects to /sign-in, the signUp and balances entries stay for keepUnusedDataFor (60 s). B signs in in the same tab within 60 s: useSignUpQuery(undefined) finds a fulfilled entry and sends no request (no refetchOnMountOrArgChange), so B sees A's profiles and A's cached balances. signUp never polls, so A's list stays for B's whole session; failed balance polls keep A's amounts in currentData. Reproduced with RTK 2.12.0 core: initiate, unsubscribe, initiate again gives 1 request and A's data. The old code kept profiles in AppShell state, which reset on unmount. Fix: clear the cache whenever authenticated becomes false (e.g. an effect in StoreProvider or AppShell calling apiSlice.util.resetApiState), or key signUp by Privy user.id; add a test. Everything else checked OK: per-profile keys with currentData and the keyed ActivityList remount; 15 s polling with skipPollingIfUnfocused plus refetchOnFocus; token per request via prepareHeaders; idempotency key per form; the active profile falls back to profiles[0], so no error flash; per-tab store; amounts stay strings; layout follows structure.md. Non-blocking: A->B->A within 60 s shows A's cached balances (with their timestamp) for up to 15 s before the next poll; the window focus event adds a refetch the old code did not make; one poll can still fire right after the tab hides, because polling.ts:105 reads the focus state from when the poll was scheduled. typecheck and the 17 unit tests pass.

2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: Fix holds. StoreProvider swaps the store with setState during render, guarded by owned.userId !== userId, so React re-runs StoreProvider before any child renders and no child reads the old store; no loop (the second pass matches). Privy (3.45.0 source) sets user and authenticated in the same batch on logout, token removal, login, session restore and cross-tab sync, so AppShell's signUp arg turns to skipToken in the same render as the swap. Scratch-copy probe under StrictMode (scratchpad only, repo untouched): load -> A gives 1 POST /v1/me with A's token and balances polling on the new store; logout gives 0 requests in 300 ms (old store's polling unsubscribed on unmount); B then gets a new POST /v1/me with B's token and B's data. Store count: 2 on mount (StrictMode init), +1 per user change. Null -> A while Privy loads is harmless: queries are skipped until ready, so nothing is lost and no extra request goes out. store-provider.test.tsx fails on the pre-fix provider (expected { profiles: [] } to be undefined) and passes with the fix. typecheck passes; 18 unit tests pass. Earlier points still hold: profileId in query args with currentData and the keyed ActivityList; LIVE_QUERY 15 s polling plus focus refetch; token read per request in prepareHeaders; one idempotency key per form; profiles[0] fallback, so no error flash. Non-blocking: (1) RTK's useQuerySubscription keeps the subscription lookup of the store it first mounted with. A direct A -> B change without passing through null leaves AppShell's signUp uninitialized (spinner until reload; no data leak). Privy always goes through null, so this cannot happen today. After the first swap the same lookup also adds one extra signUp subscription (no extra request). (2) D-47 in PROJECT.md says the cache reset on sign-out comes from the library; it now comes from the store swap. The profiles-api.test name 'forgets it all on sign-out' tests resetApiState, which app code no longer uses. (3) docs/web/structure.md still lists store/hooks.ts as an option ('as needed'), which is fine.

The test still checks the Bearer token on POST /v1/me, Idempotency-Key k-1 on the create request, that the cached signUp list becomes [personal, merchant], and that fetch was called exactly twice (no refetch). No app code uses resetApiState any more. The sign-out reset is still covered by store-provider.test.tsx. The new D-47 text matches the code: the store swap gives each signed-in user a fresh store. Earlier note (2) is resolved. pnpm --filter @forwend/web typecheck passes; pnpm --filter @forwend/web test: 5 files, 18 tests pass. Earlier non-blocking notes (1) and (3) still apply.
